newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh ex-ruler gets weapons back in hospital.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh ex-ruler gets weapons back in hospital.

text.p: Firearms seized from former Bangladesh president Hossain Mohammad Ershad have been returned to the retired general, who is in hospital after suffering chest pains, police said on Friday. "We gave the firearms back to Ershad on Thursday in his hospital," a police officer said. "This was done in pursuance of a court verdict (two years ago) that Ershad possessed the firearms legally and they should be restored to him," the officer told Reuters.

He did not say why it took so long to return the weapons. One of Ershad's aides confirmed the arms had been returned. The weapons, including three revolvers, one pistol, one rifle and one shotgun, were seized from Ershad's home in Dhaka's main army barracks in January 1991, weeks after he was deposed in an uprising on December 6, 1990, and was arrested.
He was sentenced to 10 years in prison for keeping the arms illegally but the country's High Court overturned the conviction in June 1995.

The Court said half the weapons kept by Ershad, who seized power in 1982 and became the country's longest-serving ruler, were licensed and the others were gifts that he could possess without a licence.

So his sentence was not tenable and he should be released, the court said. But Ershad was kept in prison until January 1997, when he was granted bail on 19 other charges of corruption and misuse of power. Ershad, chief of the Jatiya Party, was admitted to Dhaka's Suhrawardy Hospital on Monday after complaining of severe chest pains.
A statement issued by his press secretary on Thursday night said Ershad was still under observation.
Ershad was elected a Jatiya Party legislator in a June 1996 elections, which he contested from jail.
